newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cast protest ballots in record numbers.
newsitem.headline: French cast protest ballots in record numbers.

text.p: Record numbers of voters cast protest ballots in France's parliamentary election, supporting fringe parties -- many of them anti-European -- as a way to punish mainstream politicians, analysts said on Sunday.

"It is indisputable that in putting the National Front at the level that it is this evening, in eagerly spreading votes among the minor candidates, the French people wanted to send us a message," Gaullist National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said.
"We must hear the message, we must respond to it, and the election outcome will depend on the the quality of our response," he said on France 2 television.

Signalling widespread unhappiness with the status quo, voters gave more than 22 percent of the vote in the election's first round to minor-party candidates including the far-right National Front, ecologists and two different Trotskyite lists,

The anti-Europe vote was closer to 30 percent of the total as it included most of those minor parties plus the Euro-sceptic Communist Party, which scored nearly 10 percent and is considered a mainstream group in France.

In next Sunday's runoff, voters will have fewer opportunities for protest as most contests will include only a candidate from the governing centre-right coalition, a candidate from the mainstream left and perhaps one from the National Front.
But they can always stay home or cast a blank ballot -- traditional avenues for showing discontent in France.
Minor parties have a good reason to compete in elections in France even when they have little or no chance of winning. Their finances depend on it.
State subsidies for the parties are dished out according to the votes cast for each grouping, handed out at the rate of 11.3 francs (roughly $2) per vote.

Among the lesser known groups competing this year were the SOS Papa party, backing stronger child custody rights for divorced fathers, the Natural Law party advocating communal prayer for world peace, the Four-day Working Week party and the OSCENA party, which wants to abolish the elite National Administrative College (ENA).
